svg.title: Mind Map Studio: syncing between computers through a synced folder
svg.desc: A looping animation in three scenes. 1: an edit on this computer is written to the synced folder about 10 seconds after you stop editing, as name (id).mindmap.json with pictures in _assets; the other computer reads it when you come back to its window. 2: a project removed on one computer goes to the folder’s _trash subfolder instead of being deleted; if many files vanish at once, sync pauses and asks first. 3: when both computers changed the same project, the newer one stays and the other is kept as a conflict copy tagged conflict.
svg.text: Chrome or Edge on a computer,

g.text: Edit as usual: the project is saved in this browser.
About 10 s after you stop, it is written to the folder; pictures go to _assets/.
Each project is a normal file in a folder OneDrive (or any sync app) keeps.
so a paused OneDrive or the
A removed project goes to _trash/ in the folder; nothing is deleted outright.
Projects removed on one computer wait in the folder’s _trash subfolder.
Both computers changed the same project while apart…
The newer version stays; the other is kept as a copy tagged conflict.
If both computers changed a project, neither version is lost.
